theater: 筑前國太宰府與南九州

battle.name: 隼人叛亂
battle.theater: 筑前國太宰府與南九州
battle.brief: 720年末至721年，隼人首領間人勇率眾夜襲筑前國太宰府，殺傷官人、掠走兵器，律令朝廷集兵討平。卡面的秦連弩是漢代可連踏而發的中國弩，與本役相隔九百年，並未出現在戰場上：守軍用的是單發唐式和弩與角弓；連弩在此象徵守方本該以壓制火力固守城池，卻被奇襲打亂的防務邏輯。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 交戰的兩端，一端是奈良的律令中央政府：朝廷以大宰府作為九州的總管府，領筑前、筑後、豐前、豐後、薩摩、大隅諸國，其官署、國司、國郡的編制皆出律令，鎮西的軍馬與調度也歸它一手掌握；大宰府之下另設隼人帳，把隼人分為馬、財、造三等部曲，配屬大宰府的低階官職與雜任。另一端是南九州與琉球一帶的隼人諸首領：隼人不是單一部落，而是各自佔有山野與村落圈的群體，彼此之間沒有統一號令，平日受大宰府的國司、調役與編戶管理，也各自向琉球國的尚氏進貢。琉球尚氏此時向朝廷奉朝貢、提供隼人樂工與兵員，在叛亂中站在朝廷一邊；隼人內部也有多名首領響應朝廷而倒向官軍。這使本役始終是一場在地的、帶有族群與首領間勢力競爭色彩的內亂，而不是與任何外部勢力的交戰；朝廷的「敵人」是一群各自獨立的隼人群體，這一點直接決定了它必須以編戶、遷徙與設縣而非以常設邊軍來收束問題。
countriesEn: The two ends of this conflict were, on the one side, the ritsuryō central government of Nara: the court governed through the Dazaifu in Kyūshū, which held authority over Chikuzen, Chikugo, Buzen, Bungo, Satsuma and Ōsumi, with its offices, provincial governors and district system all created by statute, and the dispatch of troops and the remittance of the western regions in its hands; under the Dazaifu a separate hayato census (hayato chō) was kept, sorting the Hayato into three divisions — uma, zai and zō — attached to the Dazaifu's junior posts and menials. On the other side stood the Hayato chiefs of southern Kyūshū and the Ryūkyū islands: the Hayato were not a single tribe but a set of separate groups, each holding its own uplands and village circles, without a common command, and they were managed in ordinary times by the Dazaifu's officials, corvées and enrolment, while each in turn paid tribute to the Shō house of the Ryūkyū kingdom. The Shō house at this time sent tribute to the court and supplied Hayato musicians and men-at-arms, and it stood with the court during the revolt; several Hayato chiefs likewise answered the court rather than the insurgents. The result is that this remained a civil disturbance fought on the ground, coloured by ethnic identity and by the rivalry of the chiefs, and not a war with any outside power. The court's 'enemy' was a body of mutually independent Hayato groups, and that fact decided directly that the affair had to be closed by enrolment, removal and the setting up of districts rather than by a standing frontier army.
people: 叛軍的領袖是間人勇。他是隼人出身、曾入京的隼人首領，《隼人傳》一系的記錄與《續日本紀》的官府奏報都把他寫成舉兵者的核心：他在京中捲入是非，被朝廷所疑而遭遣返本鄉，返鄉之後挾著不平與本部族積下的舊怨，誘集散兵游勇，於養老年間在太宰府動手。事後他與同黨被擒，押送京師處死，這是他最為確定的結局。朝廷方面的關鍵人物是元明天皇，她於和銅四年（720）即位，是日本史上第一位以天皇身份親自統治的女皇，隼人叛亂正落在她的治世之內；內廷的實際主政者是藤原不比等，他是奈良朝政的樞紐，在《續日本紀》中就隼人亂的處置屢次上奏陳述。此外，記錄中留名的還有大宰府的奏報者——本役正是由大宰府把「隼人凶渠率眾夜襲、官人死傷、器械被掠」的消息飛騎奏上朝廷，才使事件由地方走私入國家層面的處理；以及站在朝廷一方的隼人諸將與尚氏送來的隼人兵，他們的倒向決定了叛軍在戰場上孤立的速度。
peopleEn: The leader of the insurgents was Hato Yui. He was a chief of the Hayato who had been at the capital, and both the record of the Hayato and the official memorials preserved in the Shoku Nihongi put him at the core of the rising: tangled in trouble at Kyoto and made an object of suspicion by the court, he was sent back to his own country, and returned there nursing grievances and the old enmities of his clan, gathering scattered fighters and drifting followers, and struck at the Dazaifu in the Yōrō years. He was afterwards taken with his confederates, brought under escort to the capital and put to death, and that is the most certain thing about his end. The key figure at court was Empress Yōmei, who took the throne in 720 as the first woman to rule Japan in her own right, and the Hayato revolt fell squarely within her reign; the man who actually ran the palace was Fujiwara no Fuhito, the hinge of Nara politics, who reported and gave counsel on the handling of the Hayato revolt in the Shoku Nihongi more than once. Other names in the record are the memorialists of the Dazaifu: it was the Dazaifu that sent up to the court by fast horse the news of the Hayato rebel chief leading his followers in a night attack, with officials killed and equipment carried off, and that dispatch was what carried the affair out of local hands into national handling. Then there were the Hayato chiefs who sided with the court, and the Hayato soldiers sent by the Shō house, whose choice of side decided how quickly the insurgents found themselves isolated in the field.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩是中國的發明：弩機把拉力先存起來，上弦之後不必再拉，靠踏片與撥桿自動釋放，一踩一發，可以連續射擊，用來在城頭上以壓倒性的射速把攻城者擋在牆外；這類連弩在中土的文獻可以從東漢馬援的奏議與「聚弩機」一路數到三國時曹叡、諸葛亮部下的連弩，年代都在公元前二百年之後，正合卡面所標的年份。它與七二〇年的隼人叛亂相隔近九百年，本役的戰鬥記錄裡沒有出現連弩：八世紀日本的弩是從百濟與隋唐傳入的唐式弩，機件用角或牛皮製成，一次上一發，與和弓、角弓同列於大宰府武器庫的清冊之中，與矢、刀、槊、鎧、鞍具一同供守備與出擊使用。隼人一方則以短刀、弓、槊為主，能夜行、能攀援，能在官軍作出反應之前把襲擊做完。值得留意的是，這件兵器在本役中真正的位置是一個反證：太宰府有弩、有矢、有柵門，卻因為夜襲的奇襲效果而失去了施展壓制性火力的機會，連弩式的守城邏輯正是被這一夜打破的那一套東西。
kitsEn: The Qin repeating crossbow on the card is a Chinese invention: the trigger mechanism stores the pull first, so that once the bow is drawn the string does not have to be hauled again, and a treadle with a release lever lets the stored tension go automatically, one shot per step of the tread, allowing a run of shots; its purpose was to hold the attacker outside the wall by overwhelming rate of fire from the parapet. The literature on this weapon in China runs from the memorial and the 'gathering crossbow mechanism' of the Eastern Han general Ma Yuan to the repeating crossbows of Cao Rui's and Zhuge Liang's men in the Three Kingdoms, all of them after 200 BC, which fits the year given on the card. It stands nearly nine hundred years away from the Hayato revolt of 720, and no repeating crossbow appears in the combat record of this campaign: the crossbows of eighth-century Japan were Tang-type bows inherited from Paekche and from Sui and Tang China, with mechanisms of horn or hide, cocked one shot at a time, and listed in the Dazaifu's armoury alongside the yumi, the kyū, arrows, swords, spears, armour and harness used for both garrison and field duty. The Hayato on the other side carried short swords, bows and spears, and could move by night and climb, which is what allowed them to complete their strike before the government troops could react. It is worth noticing where this weapon really stands in the campaign, and it is as a counter-example: the Dazaifu had crossbows, arrows and palisade gates, and yet the effect of a night surprise deprived it of the chance to bring its rate of fire to bear, and the defensive logic of the repeating crossbow is precisely the thing that that single night broke.
tactics: 叛軍的打法是典型的奇襲夜襲。隼人首領間人勇集合的兵力不多，記錄把骨幹人數寫在八十人上下，這樣一支隊伍靠的是速度與突然：他們在夜裡同時發動，突入太宰府的廨舍與門柵，殺傷值夜的官人，奪取武器、弓矢與其餘器械，再裹挾一部分物資退回南部山地。防守一方因此完全沒有反應時間，柵門與武器庫反而成了攻方最先取用的目標。官軍的應對是多路調兵：大宰府先遣使奏報，朝廷下令徵集筑前、筑後、豐前、豐後、薩摩、大隅諸國的兵與雜役，畿內亦出援軍，隊伍在太宰府一帶會合後分進合擊；隼人各部之間本就鬆散的聯繫在這種壓力下迅速瓦解，部分首領直接倒向朝廷，叛軍的據守點被逐個攻破，餘眾潰散於山林。戰後的處置延續了同一套邏輯：不作地毯式的搜索，而是以編戶、遷徙、設縣把隼人從原居地拆散，重新編入律令國家的人身與土地關係之中，讓「隼人是隼人」這件事從此由簿籍與郡縣來回答。
tacticsEn: The method of the insurgents was a classic surprise night attack. The force Hato Yui gathered was not large, the records putting the core of it at around eighty men, and a body of that kind relied on speed and suddenness: they struck at night all at once, forcing their way into the Dazaifu's offices and through its palisade gates, killing the officials on watch, carrying off weapons, bows, arrows and the rest of the equipment, and then withdrawing south into the hills with a share of the booty. The defenders therefore had no time at all to react, and the gates and the armoury became the first things the attackers made use of. The government response was to raise troops from many quarters: the Dazaifu sent a memorial first, the court ordered levies of fighting men and menials from Chikuzen, Chikugo, Buzen, Bungo, Satsuma and Ōsumi, with relief troops also sent from the capital provinces, and the columns were joined up in the neighbourhood of the Dazaifu and then advanced in several directions at once. The loose bonds between the various Hayato groups dissolved quickly under that pressure; several chiefs went over to the court outright, the rebel strongholds were taken one by one, and the remnants scattered into the hills. The disposition that followed carried the same logic forward: rather than searching the country inch by inch, the state broke the Hayato up by enrolment, removal and the establishment of districts, re-inserting them into the personnel and land relations of the ritsuryō state, so that the question of what a Hayato was would henceforth be answered by registers and counties.
data: 可考的數字不多，但幾個要點清楚。時間上，《續日本紀》把大宰府奏報的襲擊事件記在養老五年（721）七月，討伐在同年秋天完成；也有學者依《隼人傳》的敘述把起事推到養老三年（720）之末，卡面因此取七二〇年，而本場的月份取自奏報的七月。叛軍的骨幹規模，記錄寫在八十人上下，這個數字包含同黨的家屬，並非作戰兵力。地理上，太宰府在筑前國糟屋郡，位於今福岡縣太宰府市一帶，距京都約五百公里；距離本身意味著朝廷的援軍必須走海路或陸路，消息往返便耗去數月，這也是叛軍得以在官軍到達前擴大行動的條件。戰後的編戶數字最為具體：天平十二年（740）二月，朝廷把大宰府管內的隼人四千四百戶強行編入良民籍，分散安置到諸國；此後又有隼人被以雜役身份調往各地。隼人帳則在此前一年，即天平十一年（739），由大宰府設置，用來清點隼人戶口與調發役夫。傷亡數字在原始記錄中不詳，也不宜推算。
dataEn: The evidence for figures is thin, but several points are clear. In time, the Shoku Nihongi records the assault reported by the Dazaifu in the seventh month of Yōrō 5 (721), and the campaign against the rebels was completed in the autumn of the same year; some scholars, following the narrative of the Hayato record, push the rising back to the end of Yōrō 3 (720), which is why the card takes 720, while the month used here is the seventh month of the memorial. The size of the insurgent core is written at around eighty men, and that figure includes the families of the rebels and is not a combat strength. Geographically, the Dazaifu stood in the district of Kasuya in the province of Chikuzen, in the area of Dazaifu in Fukuoka Prefecture today, some five hundred kilometres from Kyoto; the distance itself means that any relief force had to travel by sea or by land, so that the round trip of the message took months, and that is precisely the condition that let the insurgents enlarge their action before government troops arrived. The most concrete figures belong to the aftermath: in the second month of Tenpyō 12 (740) the court forcibly enrolled 4,400 households of Hayato from the Dazaifu's jurisdiction into the register of commoners and dispersed them among the provinces; others were afterwards sent to work in other provinces as miscellaneous labour. The hayato chō itself had been set up one year earlier, in Tenpyō 11 (739), by the Dazaifu, to count Hayato households and to call up corvée labour. Casualty figures are not given in the original record and cannot responsibly be estimated.
cause: 起事的原因有兩層。表面的一層，是朝廷對隼人的處置轉變。律令國家在九州的推進，本身就是一個把山地與島嶼社會納入編戶、賦役與調發的過程；隼人被分成馬、財、造三等，配屬於大宰府及其附屬官署，國司年年照著簿籍徵發役夫與貢物，隼人首領要應付調役、追捕與各種攤派，而隼人帳一經建立，這些負擔便更精確地落到每一戶的頭上。深一層的原因是隼人首領之間的地位競爭，以及朝廷懷柔手段的副作用：間人勇是隼人之首、在京中樹敵，被朝廷疑其部族將反，於是把他遣回本鄉，令其安撫同族、勸說首領歸順。這種處置等於是把最有威望的首領送回可能起事的地方，並且公開懷疑了他；首領一旦被指為可疑，他要在自己的部落裡保住位置，就只剩下兩條路：接受中央的安撫而淪為被監視的臣民，或者乾脆把中央的懷柔轉成反叛的號召。還有一層背景是尚氏與中央的角力，隼人各部在尚氏的秩序與大宰府的律令之間本就有各自的依附方式，一旦朝廷加強攤派，兩套秩序的縫隙就容易變成戰線。
causeEn: There are two layers to the cause of the rising. The surface one is a change in how the court treated the Hayato. The ritsuryō state's advance into Kyūshū was itself a process of drawing upland and island societies into enrolment, taxation and corvée; the Hayato were sorted into the three divisions uma, zai and zō and attached to the Dazaifu and its dependent offices, and the provincial officials levied labour and tribute from them year by year, while the Hayato chiefs had to meet corvée levies, manhunts and a great variety of imposts — and once the hayato chō was established, these burdens fell on every household with a precision they had not known before. The deeper cause is the struggle for standing among the Hayato chiefs and the side effect of the court's method of conciliation: Hato Yui was a chief of the Hayato who had made enemies at Kyoto, and because the court suspected his clan of rising, it sent him back to his own country to pacify his kindred and persuade the chiefs to submit. Such a disposition amounted to returning the most prestigious chief to the one place where a rising might be organised, and it made his suspicion public. A chief once branded as suspect had only two ways left to hold his place among his own people: to accept the court's pacification and become a watched subject, or to turn the court's conciliation into the call for revolt. A further background lies in the contest between the Shō house and the centre, for the Hayato groups were attached in different ways to the Shō order and to the Dazaifu's ritsuryō order, and once the court tightened its imposts, the seam between the two systems easily became a line of battle.
impact: 這場叛亂的直接後果是隼人集團被拆散、重編。編戶與遷徙把南九州與琉球的隼人從原有的村落社會中拉出來，塞進各國的良民籍與雜役籍；四千四百戶這樣的規模意味著一個族群的整體移動。隼人縣的設置則是行政上的收束，把隼人從「異姓」的部曲轉成有固定管轄與固定調役的對象。對律令國家而言，這是一次成功的邊疆鎮壓，也是一次管理技術的升級：從大宰府直接派官管事，走向帳籍、編戶、縣置三層並用，九州的稅收與兵役從此有了更可靠的抽水口。對尚氏與琉球的關係而言，中央能平定隼人，說明尚氏對南方的主導權是被朝廷認可的，朝貢與使節往來因此更為固定，琉球在奈良朝的外交位置反而上升。對隼人本身，這一夜是族群記憶的分水嶺：此後他們雖仍被當作特殊對象編制，卻也逐步取得良民身份，隼人出身者在太宰府系統中擔任主馬、財、造之類的官職，成為律令體制裡不可忽略的一層；戰爭的物質後果則是太宰府的器械與府舍遭劫，官軍的守備編制與常備警戒被迫重整。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the revolt was that the Hayato groups were broken up and re-registered. Enrolment and removal pulled the Hayato of southern Kyūshū and the Ryūkyū islands out of the village societies they had belonged to and dropped them into the commoner registers and the labour registers of the various provinces; a movement on the scale of 4,400 households means the wholesale relocation of a people. The setting up of the Hayato district was the administrative closure of that process, turning the Hayato from retainers of a 'different surname' into a category with a fixed jurisdiction and fixed levies. For the ritsuryō state this was a successful frontier suppression and also an upgrade in administrative technique: from posting officials directly under the Dazaifu to using registers, enrolment and district jurisdiction together, so that Kyūshū's taxes and military service acquired a more reliable spout. For the Shō house and the Ryūkyū relationship, the court's ability to put down the Hayato showed that the Shō house's primacy over the south was recognised by the centre, so tribute and embassies became more regular and the Ryūkyū's diplomatic position in the Nara period actually rose. For the Hayato themselves, that night was a watershed in collective memory: from then on, though still handled as a special category, they gradually acquired commoner status, and Hayato men took posts of uma, zai and zō in the Dazaifu's establishment, becoming a layer the ritsuryō system could not do without. The material aftermath of the fighting was that the Dazaifu's equipment and offices had been looted, and the government was obliged to reorganise its garrison establishment and its standing watch.
result: 結果是朝廷方面的完全勝利。叛軍在大宰府的夜襲得手之後，未能擴大為持久戰：官軍會合後攻破其據守，間人勇與一批同黨被擒獲，押送京師後處死，餘眾或降或散，隼人諸國的武裝抵抗就此終止；太宰府的廨舍與器械雖遭掠損，國家的權威卻沒有受損，反而更被加強。善後措施隨之展開：隼人帳已設，四千四百戶隼人被編入良民，雜役調發成為固定的勞動力來源，隼人縣的設置又把手續推到法制層面，讓隼人問題從軍事事件變成行政課題。從武器的視角看，這場戰爭沒有讓任何一件兵器成名，卻把日本弩兵在守城中的侷限暴露得清清楚楚：太宰府有弩有矢，卻在奇襲的夜裡來不及架設、來不及形成射擊密度。卡面上這件更古老、更連發的秦連弩，反而正是「守城方怎樣用壓制性火力把攻擊者擋在牆外」這個命題的原型；隼人叛亂之後日本守備的調整，所走的正是提高常備警戒與射擊密度的同一條路。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete victory for the court. Having carried the Dazaifu in the night attack, the insurgents failed to turn the affair into a war of endurance: once the government columns were joined up and attacked their positions, Hato Yui and a number of his confederates were taken, brought under escort to the capital and executed, while the rest surrendered or scattered, and the armed resistance of the Hayato polities came to an end there and then. The offices and equipment of the Dazaifu had been looted, but the authority of the state was not damaged; it was strengthened instead. The measures of the aftermath followed in turn: the hayato chō was already in place, 4,400 households of Hayato had been enrolled as commoners, the calling up of menials as corvée became a fixed source of labour, and the establishment of the Hayato district carried the business on into the legal layer, turning the Hayato question from a military event into an administrative one. From the point of view of weapons, this war made no arm famous, but it laid bare with clarity the limits of the Japanese crossbowman in defence: the Dazaifu had crossbows and arrows and never got the chance to set them in place, or to achieve any density of fire, during the night of the surprise. The far older, faster-firing Qin repeating crossbow on the card is, rather, the prototype of the proposition that the defending side holds the attacker outside the wall by pressure of fire; the adjustments in Japanese defence that followed the Hayato revolt moved along exactly that line of raising the standing watch and the density of fire.
